mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLS 350d or 400d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM642 engine for the GLS 350d costs £3,800-£5,500 supply-only; a rebuilt OM656 engine for the GLS 400d costs £5,500-£7,200 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,500 depending on complexity - both V6 and straight-six work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM642 oil cooler seal failure on a Mercedes GLS 350d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A burnt-oil smell after highway driving or oil pooling in the V of the engine is the classic warning sign. The oil seals themselves are a low-cost item; the labour to replace them is the significant expense. If ignored, coolant contamination leads to bearing washout and terminal engine seizure.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLS 400d engine (OM656) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 straight-six is a modern, powerful diesel with excellent performance - 330hp and 700Nm torque. However, it has known AdBlue/SCR system issues and EGR cooler problems that can trigger warning lights and start limitations. With recalls addressed and proper maintenance, these engines are proving durable.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLS 350d and 400d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 V6 diesels routinely reach 150,000-200,000+ miles before major work. The OM656 straight-six is too new for definitive long-term data, but with AdBlue issues addressed, similar longevity is expected.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLS 350d or 400d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLS is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical or transmission faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £3,800-£5,500 - far less than replacing a £15,000-£30,000 vehicle. The GLS 400d's higher value (£35,000-£60,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLS 350d or 400d need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres; the OM656 straight-six requires approximately 7.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLS Class 350d/400d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLS 350d launched with the X166 generation in 2013 as the UK's best-selling full-size luxury diesel SUV, powered by the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel producing 258hp. In 2019, the all-new X167 GLS 400d replaced it with the OM656 3.0-litre straight-six diesel - a more powerful, more refined, and more efficient engine that represented a major engineering shift from V6 to inline-six architecture.

milestones.description: 2019 - OM642.826 continues as the GLS 350d; also offered as 249hp variant
Facelift X167; OM656 continues with refined AdBlue and emissions systems

items.title: 3.0L V6 Diesel (2013-2019)
items.commonFailure: Oil cooler seal deterioration and timing chain guide wear - the OM642 V6 is a robust workhorse but has well-documented weak points. Oil cooler seals in the V6 valley harden with heat cycling, causing external leaks that can lead to low oil pressure if ignored. Timing chain tensioner wear can also cause cold-start rattling on high-mileage units. Typical failure mileage: 60,000-90,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLS Class 350d/400d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLS 350d's OM642 V6 and the GLS 400d's OM656 straight-six are both fundamentally robust diesel engines, but each has well-documented weaknesses that drive replacement decisions. The OM642's V6 suffers from oil cooler seal failures - a £10 part that costs £900 in labour to replace. The OM656's advanced emissions systems can be problematic, with AdBlue and EGR issues driving replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal & Timing Chain Wear
problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal & Timing Chain Wear - The V6 Diesel's Expensive Weakness
problems.rootCause: The OM642's oil cooler sits in the tight valley between the V6 cylinder banks. Factory rubber seals harden with heat cycling, allowing oil to pool in the valley or drip onto the exhaust, producing a burnt-oil smell. Timing chain tensioner wear can also cause cold-start rattling. The seals themselves are a low-cost item - the labour is the significant expense.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine valley access, remove intake crossover, turbo and swirl manifold; replace with upgraded Viton seals
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no other damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioner, rails
Complete V6 swap with upgraded seals and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil contamination or timing failure has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2019 GLS 350d 4MATIC is worth approximately £15,000-£30,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLS 350d sits in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples with good bodywork and transmission health.
problems.recommendation: The OM642 oil leak is progressive, not sudden. If caught early during routine servicing - oil pooling in the valley or a burnt-oil smell after highway driving - the specialist seal overhaul at £900-£1,400 extends engine life affordably. Once coolant has entered the oil pan or metallic debris is present, patch repairs are futile. For high-mileage GLS 350d models, a rebuilt OM642 with upgraded Viton seals delivers superior long-term value and peace of mind - specialist pricing of £3,800-£5,500 is significantly lower than dealer rates.

problems.group: OM656 AdBlue System & EGR Cooler Failure
problems.h4: OM656 AdBlue System & EGR Cooler Failure - The Straight-Six Diesel's Emissions Challenge
problems.rootCause: The OM656's selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system uses a heated AdBlue tank, dosing pump and NOx sensors. Crystallisation of urea fluid or heater element burnout causes blockages, triggering countdown warnings and eventual engine start prevention. The EGR system can also suffer from carbon build-up, while turbo actuator hose failure has been reported.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan of SCR system, tank, dosing module, NOx sensors
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms which component has failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue heater pump, flush tank, recalibrate dosing pump
repairOptions.longevity: If crystallisation or heater failure is confirmed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tank, dosing module, NOx sensors and update ECU software
repairOptions.longevity: Comprehensive emissions fix; removes start limits

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 with updated emission components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If emissions issues have caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-present GLS 400d 4MATIC is worth approximately £35,000-£60,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLS 400d sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: AdBlue faults are primarily emission-system issues, not core mechanical failures. If your GLS 400d still runs smoothly but displays a countdown warning, a specialist SCR overhaul is significantly cheaper and entirely sufficient. However, if the fault has triggered repeated limp modes and high soot accumulation, the DPF and turbo are often compromised. In that scenario, a rebuilt engine with integrated emission components provides a complete reset. Check for any outstanding Mercedes recalls on OM656 engines - some units are subject to coolant pump vacuum circuit recalls.

problems.group: OM656 Turbocharger Actuator & Rough Idle Issues
problems.h4: OM656 Turbocharger Actuator & Rough Idle Issues
problems.rootCause: The OM656's turbo actuator hose can fail due to heat exposure, causing the hose to collapse and affecting boost response. Rough idle has also been reported when the air conditioning compressor is engaged or when in gear with the foot on the brake.

repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether actuator or hose is the cause

problems.recommendation: If you experience rough idle or loss of power on your GLS 400d, have a specialist inspect the turbo actuator system immediately. The actuator hose is a known weakness and replacement at £250-£450 is significantly cheaper than a full turbocharger replacement. If the turbo has already failed, a rebuilt OM656 with new turbo components is the only safe option - on a GLS 400d worth £35,000-£60,000, this is a justifiable investment.
